citation.authors: Ramesh D, Haney M, Cooper ZD
citation.title: Marijuana's dose-dependent effects in daily marijuana smokers
citation.retrieval_method: full HTML text fetched directly from PMC article viewer (pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov), verified as complete article (abstract through references, all 5 figure captions and both tables present)

ramesh-2013.setting: New York State Psychiatric Institute, outpatient laboratory; part of a larger 8-session naltrexone/marijuana interaction study (only placebo-naltrexone sessions reported here)
ramesh-2013.analysis_note: 19 participants completed the study; data from 1 volunteer excluded due to experimental error, leaving N=18 for analysis
ramesh-2013.population: non-treatment-seeking daily marijuana smokers, 21-45 years old
ramesh-2013.inclusion_criteria: smoking >=3 marijuana cigarettes 4x/week for the prior month; healthy per physical exam/ECG/blood chemistry; marijuana use confirmed by urine toxicology and self-report; no repeated use of other drugs (except nicotine/alcohol/caffeine); no current DSM-IV-TR Axis I psychopathology; females excluded if pregnant/nursing/not using contraception

demographics.other_notes: 7 participants reported daily cigarette smoking (4.9 +/- 0.9 cigarettes/day); 10 reported drinking alcohol weekly (2.0 +/- 0.2 days/week, 2.7 +/- 0.4 drinks/occasion)

ramesh-2013.condition_detail: Every session, participants smoked 6 total puffs from 3 marijuana cigarettes (2 puffs/cigarette, 5-s inhale, 10-s hold, 40-s interpuff interval). The number of ACTIVE vs inactive cigarettes varied by condition: 0 puffs = 3 inactive cigarettes; 2 puffs = 1 active + 2 inactive; 4 puffs = 2 active + 1 inactive; 6 puffs = 3 active. Active puffs were always smoked before inactive puffs within a session. Randomized within-subject design; all participants exposed to all 4 conditions.

product.note: Due to limited supply of the 6.2% THC stock, the first 13 participants smoked 6.2% THC active cigarettes and the final 5 smoked 5.5% THC; strength was held consistent within each participant across their sessions.

outcome_domains: expired carbon monoxide (CO, Bedfont Micro Smokerlyzer)
MRF: strength, good effect, bad effect, liking, take-again (5-item VAS)
SE-VAS: 44-item mood/physical-symptom VAS incl. 'high', 'stimulated', 'I want marijuana'
task battery: repeated acquisition, divided attention (DAT), digit-symbol substitution (DSST), digit recall (DRT)
amount of marijuana smoked (pre/post cigarette weight difference)
ramesh-2013.statistics_method: Repeated-measures ANOVA with planned comparisons, Huynh-Feldt corrected; significance threshold p<=.05; six planned pairwise comparisons per dependent variable (0v2, 0v4, 0v6, 2v4, 2v6, 4v6 active puffs)
